_comment: Ledger of user-visible fixes and the tokens that prove each one is compiled
into a shipped artifact. Read by tools/ship/verify_fix_manifest.py.
Why this exists: a package was once handed over whose fixes were absent,
because the fixes were still sitting in unmerged PRs. The build succeeded,
the installer installed, and nothing in the pipeline could tell the
difference. A fix is not shipped until a token from it is found inside the
- Quote-agnostic. The materialized document is embedded as JSON with
backslash-escaped quotes, so a token containing a literal double quote
will not match even when the code is present.
- Discriminating. A token must not already exist on the commit BEFORE the
fix, or it proves nothing. Check with:
- Stable. Prefer an identifier the fix introduces over prose a later

A token must discriminate INSIDE THE BINARY, not merely inside the document. The binary also contains Skia, Pulp and the C++ sources, so a word that is absent from the document can still be abundant in the artifact: 'subpath' reads 0 in the pre-fix document and 18 in the pre-fix binary, and would have reported a fix as shipped on a build that predates it. Screen every candidate against a binary built BEFORE the fix and require zero.

Not every fix is binary-token-verifiable, and the manifest says so rather than inventing a token. A change made purely of style values leaves no identifier behind, and a removal leaves nothing to find at all. Those rows carry 'verifiable': false with the reason, and the tool reports them as NOT-PROVABLE so they are visible rather than silently uncovered.

fixes.title: Reopening the preset manager shows every preset again
fixes.note: Comment tokens rather than identifiers: the fix adds an effect keyed on [open] whose only code is calls that already existed, so the surrounding rationale is the sole new text. It fails closed - a reword breaks the gate loudly and the manifest gets updated.

fixes.title: The preset name in the detail pane is no longer clipped
fixes.reason: The fix is style values on an existing node - no new identifier and no new text reaches the binary. Verify by opening a preset whose name is long and reading it whole.

fixes.title: Preset rows no longer show a shortcut-looking F / U chip
fixes.reason: A removal, and it removed markup rather than any identifier, so there is nothing to find and nothing whose absence is specific. Verify by opening the preset list and seeing no chip.

fixes.title: The morph slider moves the viewport, not just the bands
Every preset-dropdown row caption sits on one column
The response curve breaks at a muted band instead of plunging through it
Cmd-Shift drag adds to and removes from the marquee selection
Double-click and Return apply a preset and close the manager
EDIT MODE shortcut chips show S/L/B/F/G and the letters work
fixes.note: Shipped before the current installed build, so this row reads PRESENT on an older package. That is deliberate: a manifest in which every row can only ever read ABSENT cannot distinguish a stale package from a broken instrument.

fixes.title: Dismissing an overlay follows one policy in every host (Pulp SDK)
fixes.note: Screened against the pre-fix binaries built on the v0.847.0 SDK (which provably lacks ae0514a6b): both read 0 there. 'data-overlay' was REJECTED as a candidate - it already reads 9 pre-fix. 'setOverlayTrigger' is a register_bridge_function name literal; a control over seven pre-existing bridge names (setFaderSkin, createVirtualGrid, ...) confirmed such literals reach the Mach-O at 1-3 occurrences each.

fixes.title: An opening popup no longer shows a second, unasked-for keyboard cursor (Pulp SDK)
fixes.note: Identifiers from core/view/js/web-compat-document.js, which is embedded verbatim in the document; a control on neighbouring pre-existing identifiers (activeIndex=11, requestAnimationFrame=45) confirms that file reaches the binary. All three read 0 in the pre-fix binaries.

fixes.title: A remounted subtree keeps its authored child order (Pulp SDK)
fixes.reason: No token can discriminate this one. The only new literal is 'insertChild', and the shipped React host-config ALREADY emits a feature-detected call for it: the pre-fix binaries contain a `typeof g4.insertChild === function` guard around a call2('insertChild', ...) and read insertChild=2 with no SDK implementation behind it. Adopting that token would certify the fix as shipped on a build that predates it. Verify by reopening a dropdown and seeing its rows keep their authored order.

fixes.title: Plugin bundles carry an app icon (Pulp SDK)
fixes.reason: The change is CMake plus Info.plist templates plus an .icns resource; nothing new reaches the executable, so a Mach-O strings check is the wrong instrument. Verify per bundle with CFBundleIconFile in Contents/Info.plist and the matching .icns in Contents/Resources.

fixes.title: A dropdown re-opened after a preset apply or snapshot recall keeps its authored row order
fixes.note: Spectr-side companion to the SDK's widget-bridge-child-order row, which no token can prove. This one is provable because the renderer gained real identifiers: attach() computed an insert index and dropped it on the floor when calling materialize(). Screened against BOTH pre-fix binaries (the installed 06:24 build from 769a596, and the Sep-12 22:32 build on the v0.847.0 SDK): both read 0. 'materializeUnder' was REJECTED as a candidate - it reads 4 pre-fix, because the function already existed and the fix only added its index parameter.

fixes.title: Opening a second dropdown while one is open takes one press, not two
fixes.note: Tokens from Spectr's own runtime.js, deliberately NOT the SDK's 'setOverlayTrigger': that literal reads 3 in the installed pre-fix build (which already carries the v0.850.0 SDK) and 0 only in the older v0.847.0 build, so it proves the SDK shipped the verb - not that Spectr calls it. 'aria-haspopup' was REJECTED at 9 pre-fix, 'Scoped' at 2 and 'counterpart' at 1. '_isTrigger' is the local that decides the mark; 'unmarks' is comment prose and fails closed on a reword, which is the documented bargain.

fixes.title: The `?` popover offers Learn more, which opens a scrollable guide
fixes.note: Three tokens triangulating the three halves of the feature: the overlay component, the control that routes into it, and the global the copy is assigned to. The copy ships as its own embedded asset (native-ui/materialized/help-content.js, added to SPECTR_NATIVE_ASSET_SOURCES) rather than inlined into the document, so SPECTR_HELP_TEXT also proves that asset reached the binary. All three read 0 in both pre-fix binaries.

fixes.title: The morph's "unavailable" reason sits in a caption below the slider, not inside its groove
fixes.note: Nearly filed unprovable. A word-level diff of the document across this commit adds and removes nothing, which is true and misleading: the caption was REWORDED as it moved, 'SET B' -> 'SET B TO MORPH', and the new word is two characters long so a token scan with a sane minimum length steps straight over it. The control is the good one - the OLD wording 'SET A + B' reads 1 in both pre-fix binaries while every 'TO MORPH' variant reads 0, so the instrument demonstrably reaches that exact string region and the absence is the fix's, not the reader's. What this token proves is that the commit is compiled in; the move out of the 90x16 groove to a caption at top:20 carries no identifier of its own and rides along with the rewording, which shipped in the same change.

fixes.title: All four Spectr bundles carry the product icon
fixes.reason: CMake plus Info.plist plus an .icns resource; nothing new reaches the executable, so a Mach-O strings check is the wrong instrument. Verify per bundle with a non-empty CFBundleIconFile in Contents/Info.plist and the matching .icns in Contents/Resources. Note what this does NOT buy: CFBundleIconFile is inert on a .vst3/.component/.clap - only the .app gets a Finder icon from it. The plugin rows are for correctness and future hosts, not a visible icon today.

fixes.title: SHORTCUTS spells every modifier the same way - CMD / SHIFT / ALT, no glyphs
fixes.note: Also nearly filed unprovable, on the reasoning that a glyph-to-word substitution only REMOVES text and that the word CMD is three characters in a 44 MB Mach-O. Both halves are true and the conclusion still did not follow: the two rewritten chips are contiguous strings, CMD+DRAG and CMD+SHIFT+DRAG, and a token may contain any character except a double quote. Both read 0 in the pre-fix binaries against a DRAG control that reads 5 there, so the instrument reaches the chip strings and the absence belongs to the fix. Scope, because the row should not be read as more than it is: this is the twelve-row SHORTCUTS panel only. One glyph chip survives elsewhere on purpose - the preset dropdown's MANAGE row still reads U+21E7 U+2318 P - and it was never in this fix's scope.

fixes.title: SCULPT / PEAK / PRESET and OVERFLOW keep their own layout once snapshots A and B are both captured
fixes.note: Both identifiers are new in native-ui/materialized/runtime.js, which CMakeLists embeds via SPECTR_NATIVE_ASSET_SOURCES alongside the document - so runtime.js-only tokens do reach the Mach-O. Screened against both pre-fix binaries (the installed 12:43 build and the Sep-12 22:32 build): 0 and 0. The control is the state this fix demotes, 'snapshots-morph', which reads 1 in both, so the reader demonstrably reaches the captured-state atlas and the absence belongs to the fix. What the tokens prove is that the level-fallback resolution shipped: a state whose selector describes a session-long LEVEL is now a fallback rather than a winner over an open surface. Before it, the permanent data-spectr-snapshots-ready marker shadowed every dropdown's own captured state from the second capture until relaunch, and the option rows lost the bindings that stack them.

fixes.title: The guide's close button sits inside a box a press can actually land in
fixes.note: The anchor shipped as a 0x0 box, which paints correctly and cannot be touched: Rect::contains is half-open, so a 0x0 rect contains no point at any coordinate. Both tokens read 0 in both pre-fix binaries against a 'zIndex: 60' control - the guide's own scrim, inside this anchor - that reads 1 in the 12:43 build. READ THIS ROW NARROWLY. It proves the anchor now has a real box at zIndex 70 whose rect covers the close button; it does NOT prove a press lands on it, because no instrument in this repo can deliver a native press. SPECTR_CLICK dispatches a synthetic DOM click and bypasses hit-testing entirely, which is the same blindness that let the 0x0 anchor ship green. Verify by hand: open the guide and click the x.

fixes.title: The band readout stops painting over the guide, and the cursor arrows while it is open and restores on dismiss
fixes.reason: No token exists because the fix adds no code. Both behaviours are consequences of the anchor regaining a real box: hover and wheel hit-test the tree directly rather than consulting the overlay slot, so an untouchable anchor let the pointer reach the band surface underneath, which kept updating its readout and holding its editing cursor. Restoring the box restores the ordinary tree walk, which makes the band surface's EXISTING onPointerLeave fire - and that one handler already clears the readout and returns the cursor to an arrow, then restores hover-driven cursors when the guide unmounts. A row whose entire implementation is 'the pre-existing handler is now reachable' has nothing new to find. It ships with help-guide-anchor-reachable above and stands or falls with it. Verify by hand: open the guide, move the pointer across it, and confirm the readout does not paint through and the cursor is an arrow; dismiss it and confirm hover cursors come back.

fixes.title: Learn more sits below the thirteen shortcut rows instead of printing across the first two
fixes.note: These tokens are CAPTURE GEOMETRY and are coupled to the shortcut row count, so adding a row moves them and this row reads ABSENT on a build that still carries the fix. That is what happened here: #125 appended a thirteenth row, and the Learn more button moved from button index 13 top 327.859375 to index 14 top 351.15625 while the panel grew from height 374.059375 to 397.35625 -- both by 23.296875, one row pitch, which is the measured pitch #125 reports. The old pair still reads 1 each in the pre-fix binary and the new pair reads 0 there, so the row discriminates in both directions. When the next row lands, re-measure rather than assuming a regression: the control is that the button entry still exists at all.

fixes.title: The guide is titled About Spectr
fixes.note: The token carries its markdown hash on purpose. Bare 'About Spectr' was REJECTED at 2 pre-fix in the 12:43 build, and the two occurrences say exactly why: they are the overlay's FALLBACK title and its aria-label, both shipped in #115. Adopting it would certify this rename against a build that predates it while actually proving the previous PR. The heading is the one place the rename happened - help-content.js, embedded as its own asset - and '# About Spectr' reads 0 in both pre-fix binaries. The control is the old heading, '# What Spectr does', which reads 1 in the 12:43 build and 0 in the post-fix source, so the reader reaches that exact string region.

fixes.title: The guide offers a copy control that confirms with Copied
fixes.note: Four tokens for the four halves that have to all be present for the button to work: the plain-text extractor (so a paste receives prose, not '## Zooming' and '**Sculpt**'), the button's own marker, the native bridge verb, and the label the user actually sees. All four read 0 in both pre-fix binaries. 'clipboard_write' is new in BOTH the document and src/editor_bridge.cpp and is Spectr's own verb, not the SDK's - the trap this manifest already records under dropdown-switch-one-press. Two candidates were REJECTED and both are instructive. 'Copy failed' reads 2 pre-fix, and neither is ours: they are Dawn's 'Copy failed, draw pass dropped!' and 'Copy failed to generate mipmaps' - the exact shape of the 'subpath' trap, a string absent from the document and abundant in the binary. 'setCopyState' reads 4 pre-fix because the Settings build-info button already owns one. 'Copied' survives only because that older button spells its labels in caps (COPY / COPYING) while the guide's are title case; a later pass that unifies the casing will break this row loudly, which is the intended failure.

fixes.title: A recall or sweep no longer flashes every band it carries back across the mute threshold
fixes.note: The flourish is now gated on its source: commitGain/commitMany take a `replay` flag and only an operator gesture lights the pulse. `unmutePulseRef` alone is NOT a token - it reads 8 in the pre-fix binary, because the ref already existed and only its guard is new.

fixes.title: Mute or unmute a whole band selection with `m`
fixes.note: The ref mirror is part of the fix, not incidental: the bank object is rebuilt on [N, snapshots, view, onNativeState] and NOT on selection, so a bank method closing over `selection` reads the empty mount-time Set forever. `mutedGainDbRef` is NOT a token - it reads 18 in the pre-fix binary.

fixes.title: Clear a snapshot slot, and RESET ALL now clears all three things it advertises
fixes.note: The handler is the substance and it earns its place without any gesture: RESET ALL advertised `gains . view . snapshots` and cleared two of the three, because the editor dropped its mirror while the processor kept both slots populated and the next projection re-lit the dots. `CLEARED` and `nativeOwnsSnapshots` are NOT tokens - they read 3 and 4 in the pre-fix binary.

fixes.title: A muted band stays silent and still while an LFO modulates morph
fixes.reason: NO TOKEN CAN PROVE THIS, and the absence was measured rather than assumed. The fix is pure control flow in C++ - three gates and a loop in Spectr::process plus an inline guard in modulation.hpp - and it introduces no string literal at all: the only quoted text anywhere in the diff sits inside comments, which never reach a binary. The shipped Mach-O is also stripped of C++ symbols, so identifiers cannot stand in for literals: 'preserve_authored_mutes', 'apply_modulation_to_target' and 'AudioModulationState' each read 0 in BOTH the pre-fix and the post-fix binary, and 'morph_derived' / 'morph_overrides' read 1 in BOTH because they are pre-existing state-serialisation keys - adopting either would certify the fix as shipped on the build that predates it. A full string-set diff of the two Spectr.app executables (1c86c3b vs d6f0b86) leaves exactly one meaningful new string, the baked source SHA, which dates the build rather than proving the fix and would go stale on the next commit. PROVEN INSTEAD BY BEHAVIOUR, which is stronger than a string match: tools/spectr-detectors/modulation_preserves_authored_mute.py compiles a probe against the real headers and passes 12 destination x depth rows, while all five planted wrong implementations (no-preservation, morph-only, flag-only, strobe, dead-modulation) are rejected, so the suite demonstrably can fail. The Catch2 cases named in tools/ci/acceptance-ctest-patterns.txt prove the same invariant end to end through Spectr::process. VERIFY BY HAND: capture snapshots A and B, mute a band, assign an LFO to morph and let it run - the muted band must neither sound nor move, and its mute badge must stay over a flat bar.

fixes.title: A band edited after both snapshots are captured keeps the edit instead of snapping back to snapshot A
fixes.reason: NO TOKEN CAN PROVE THIS, and the absence was measured rather than assumed. The fix is pure control flow in C++ - three gates and a loop in Spectr::process plus an inline guard in modulation.hpp - and it introduces no string literal at all: the only quoted text anywhere in the diff sits inside comments, which never reach a binary. The shipped Mach-O is also stripped of C++ symbols, so identifiers cannot stand in for literals: 'preserve_authored_mutes', 'apply_modulation_to_target' and 'AudioModulationState' each read 0 in BOTH the pre-fix and the post-fix binary, and 'morph_derived' / 'morph_overrides' read 1 in BOTH because they are pre-existing state-serialisation keys - adopting either would certify the fix as shipped on the build that predates it. A full string-set diff of the two Spectr.app executables (1c86c3b vs d6f0b86) leaves exactly one meaningful new string, the baked source SHA, which dates the build rather than proving the fix and would go stale on the next commit. PROVEN INSTEAD BY BEHAVIOUR, which is stronger than a string match: tools/spectr-detectors/modulation_preserves_authored_mute.py compiles a probe against the real headers and passes 12 destination x depth rows, while all five planted wrong implementations (no-preservation, morph-only, flag-only, strobe, dead-modulation) are rejected, so the suite demonstrably can fail. The Catch2 cases named in tools/ci/acceptance-ctest-patterns.txt prove the same invariant end to end through Spectr::process. This row is the same merge's other user-visible half: the audio path derived the field from the bank whenever both slots were populated, while morph defaults to 0.0, so capturing the second snapshot silently replaced the authored field with snapshot A and every later band edit was discarded on the next block. VERIFY BY HAND: capture A and B, then drag any band - the new level must persist instead of reverting.

fixes.title: The About guide scrolls without re-committing the whole editor tree
fixes.note: Two tokens, one per half of the fix, and both are the substance rather than a marker beside it. The offset was React state, so one wheel sample was one commit, and any commit that dirties the materialized tree re-applies the WHOLE captured atlas before the layout pass behind it. The offset now goes straight to the two nodes that move -- the content's marginTop and the scrollbar thumb's top -- neither of which any captured binding describes; that is the first token. The second is the body memo: the component rebuilt ~90 spans from the 3.8 KB source text on every sample, none of it dependent on the offset. MEASURED, 48 samples through the host's own deliver_mouse_wheel on the built standalone: p50 20.166 / 20.413 / 20.221 ms before, 0.023 / 0.025 / 0.024 ms after, corroborated by Perfetto at 658 bridge calls per sample before and 2 after, with dom_event_dispatch at 48 in BOTH arms as the control that the same work was driven either way. SCREENED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS against the shipping document: both tokens read 0 at d6f0b86 (the merge before #130) and 1 at e66d901, while the controls data-spectr-help-guide-panel and data-spectr-help-scroll-content read 1 in both -- so a zero is the token being absent and not the instrument being broken. Their predecessors 'var [scrollTop, setScrollTop] = React.useState(0);' and 'var blocks = spectrHelpBlocks();' read 1 before and 0 after, which is the same discrimination from the other side. Both are single-line printable ASCII, so they survive `strings -a` over the embedded document.

fixes.title: The guide button's caption sits in the middle of its box instead of at the top of it
fixes.note: The token is the nested caption span's own marker, and the NESTING is the mechanism -- not a label attached beside it. This panel is laid out from its capture, and fillCapturedCaption2 re-pins any captured-box node's caption position:absolute with all four insets 0; a Label defaults to TextVerticalAlign::top, so the text sat at the top of a 31.2px box whose own ink is 15.2px tall. Adding alignItems:center to the button changed nothing and this was measured, not assumed: the ink stayed at 769.800..777.800 to the pixel. Making the caption nested markup is what fixes it -- asText(props.children) becomes undefined, the stub caption becomes a zero-contribution overlay, and the authored span is a real flex child of a Row that was already centring its children. So this marker is present exactly when the fix is. NOT KEYED ON THE CAPTION TEXT: the button was renamed from 'Learn more' to 'About Spectr' in the same package, so a row keyed on that string would have gone absent on a build that carries the fix -- the failure mode this ledger exists to catch, not to fall into. SCREENED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS against the shipping document: 0 at d6f0b86 (the merge before #130), 1 at e66d901, and still 1 after the rename, with data-spectr-help-guide-panel and data-spectr-help-scroll-content at 1 in all three as the control. 'data-spectr-help-learn-more' is NOT the token -- it is the BUTTON's marker, shipped by #115, and reads 1 in the pre-fix binary too, so adopting it would certify this fix as present on a build that predates it. Single-line printable ASCII, so it survives `strings -a` over the embedded document.

fixes.title: A right-click reaches its onContextMenu handler, with the press coordinates
fixes.note: Pulp SDK fix reached by the SDK repin. Tokens are the emitted-JS literals the bridge builds for registerContextMenu; both read 0 in the pre-repin binary while registerContextMenu itself reads 1, so the region is present and the tokens discriminate. Behaviourally confirmed: the context-menu census in Spectr-native-shot goes from 0 views carrying on_context_menu under the old SDK to 5 under this one, and route_context_press reports handled=yes.

fixes.title: Home and End move the context-menu cursor to the first and last selectable row
fixes.reason: A C++ member function (ContextMenu::move_hover_to_edge), and C++ method names do not survive into this binary's strings: the pre-existing fire_close, move_hover and on_key_event all read 0 while the class names ContextMenu and ComboBox read 8 and 7. A token here would read ABSENT on a build that carries the fix. Verify by opening a context menu and pressing Home and End.

fixes.title: A control marked aria-haspopup counts as an overlay trigger, so switching menus takes one press
fixes.note: Pulp SDK fix reached by the repin. aria-haspopup, _reevaluateOverlay and __replayAriaAttributes__ all read NON-zero pre-fix (11, 8, 12) and prove nothing; ariaPopup is the identifier the fix introduces and reads 0 pre-fix.

fixes.title: The CLAP plug-in bundle declares itself as a package by shipping PkgInfo
fixes.reason: Adds a file to the bundle rather than code to the binary, so no token can exist. Verify with: test -f <Spectr.clap>/Contents/PkgInfo

fixes.title: A gate that presses a control at the rect it paints and fails when nothing lands there
fixes.reason: Ships no application code -- it adds tools/native_shot.cpp, a detector and a workflow gate, none compiled into the shipped bundles. Its value is that it verifies OTHER fixes: it is the instrument behind the context-menu census.

fixes.title: The band menu's unmute gives back the level it took away
fixes.note: Screened in both directions against the materialized document: 0 at c2f35eb (the merge before #135) and 3 at 05be32b, with spectrShortcutChipStyle reading 4 as the control in both arms. The identifier is the one the fix introduces to stash and restore the pre-mute gain, so it discriminates rather than keying on a pre-existing string.

fixes.title: The band menu offers Select all, Select none and Mute / Unmute selection
fixes.note: Same two-arm screen: both read 0 at c2f35eb and 3 at 05be32b against a control of 4.

fixes.title: The Latency control: choose Tracking or Mixing in Settings
fixes.note: Screened in both directions against BINARIES, not the document: both read 0 in the pre-change Spectr build at d2759a6 and non-zero after (1 and 2), with SpectrSettingsGroup reading 2 in both arms as the control. Both identifiers are introduced by this change, so they discriminate rather than keying on a pre-existing string. Deliberately NOT render_mode: it reads 2 in BOTH arms (it occurs in Pulp/Skia text the binary already carried), which is exactly the 'absent from the document, abundant in the artifact' trap this manifest's own header warns about.
